one_month_reasoning: No DOCN-specific event is scheduled inside the window. The Q3 2026 date is not announced, and EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 history (Q3 prints 2022-11-07, 2023-11-02, 2024-11-04, 2025-11-05; source 31) puts it after the last in-window close of Fri 2026-10-30, with roughly 95% probability. The residual risk is a pre-announcement, as on 2026-07-07 (source 18). Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 prints (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META, late October) with capex and AI-capacity commentary, which move the neocloud group DOCN trades with. These are two-sided: a capex raise is bullish for demand and bearish for financing sentiment. I have no directional edge, so the distribution is a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $139.3 (a hair below spot for post-run-up mean reversion) with monthly sigma 22.5% (82%/sqrt(12) ~23.7%, trimmed slightly because the earnings day falls outside the window).

fair_value.method: A blend of 38x CY2028E EPS of $2.40 ($91), 16x NTM EBITDA of $0.95B less $1.1B horizon net debt ($113), and a DCF rolled forward to Oct-2027 ($118; 11% WACC, 4% terminal growth, consensus-level 2027 revenue, lease-funded capex in FCF). Weights 35/30/35 give ~$107, versus $140 spot (78x CY27 street EPS).

Infrastructure-peer CY2027 median is 23.7x (7 names; 23.4x per the supervisor recompute), and the 10 profitable peers range from 14.5x to 209x. The premium uses PEG parity: infrastructure peers trade at ~1.2-1.4x PEG on ~15-20% EPS growth, and 1.2 x DOCN's ~31-33% contracted EPS growth gives ~38-40x. I take the low end because gross margin is falling and growth is lease-funded. Above 40x would need evidence I do not have.

bear.story: AI ARR growth slows as GPU-hour pricing for mainstream cards (H100/H200 in a tight or falling band) rolls over and larger neoclouds/hyperscalers undercut inference pricing. 2027 growth lands at 30-35% vs the >50% target, MUFG lease draws push net debt toward $1.5B, and the multiple falls to ~30x a lower ~$1.85 2028 EPS (near the infrastructure peer range).

base.story: Industry demand stays capacity-constrained through 2027 (hyperscaler capex ~$1T, CRWV backlog, Akamai GPUs sold out), and DOCN roughly meets the $1.81B consensus. EPS grows ~33% to ~$2.40 for 2028, and the multiple de-rates from 78x to ~55x NTM, still above my 38x fair multiple because the market keeps an AI-growth premium. The stock ends slightly below spot.

bull.story: Inference compounds (inference +~800% y/y, $1M+ customer ARR +214%) and 2028 tracks the thin +48% MarketScreener consensus ($2.69B revenue, $1.11B EBITDA). 2028 EPS reaches ~$3.2 and the market keeps ~75x, so the stock breaks the $187.50 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: CY2027 street (non-GAAP) EPS from one source (Finviz, 2026-10-02). MSFT and ORCL are calendarized; Jan-FY names use FY Jan-28 as CY27. No stockanalysis 'Forward PE' and no GAAP multiples. Infrastructure anchor (AKAM, NET, FSLY, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, ORCL): 14.5x-209x, median 23.7x (interquartile ~16-41x). All 10 profitable peers including the developer-software sensitivity names (DDOG, MDB, SNOW): median 32.5x. CRWV and NBIS are loss-making on CY27 (P/E n/m). EV/EBITDA: CY27 consensus EBITDA was retrievable only for CRWV (7.53x). The 14x infrastructure/neocloud median comes from the supervisor's recompute (source 30) and is not re-verified by me. DOCN today: ~78x CY27 street EPS of ~$1.80; ~23x EV/CY27 EBITDA (EV ~$16.7B with $0.28B net debt / ~$0.73B MarketScreener CY27 consensus EBITDA).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 38x NTM (CY2028) EPS: about 60% above the 23.7x infrastructure median and inside the 14.5-209x range, below FSLY/MDB and the high-multiple software names. 16x NTM EV/EBITDA: about 2 turns above the ~14x infrastructure/neocloud median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium is growth-adjusted, not a sector-outperformance call. Infrastructure peers trade at ~1.2-1.4x PEG on ~15-20% EPS growth. DOCN's EPS growth is ~31% from the FY26 guide midpoint to the CY27 street figure, and ~33% into 2028. That growth is contracted: RPO is $894M, with $366M recognisable within 12 months, and multi-year nine-figure AI commitments run on committed capacity coming online through 2027-28. NTM growth at the Oct-2027 horizon should therefore still be ~30%, which makes the premium persistent through the horizon. PEG 1.2 x ~32% gives ~38-40x, and I take the low end because gross margin is falling (60%->55%), capex is lease-funded (MUFG facility) and EPS growth lags revenue growth. I give no premium beyond PEG parity: the developer-software multiples (DDOG/SNOW/NET at 94-209x) rest on 75-80% gross margins and no GPU capex, which DOCN does not have.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$78 (~43x CY2027 street EPS, close to the $77 March 2026 offering price, and under half the August high), the price would most likely reflect a fundamental break rather than volatility: AI customer ARR deceleration, a guide-down from the >50% 2027 growth target, failure to convert the $894M RPO, GPU-hour price deflation hitting AI pricing, or a dilutive raise because lease-funded capex outran cash flow. With corrected net debt (~$0.28B), the core cloud plus a modest AI business is worth roughly $75-85 on infrastructure-peer multiples with a small growth premium.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established that my net debt was stale: $471.8M of 2030 notes were retired on 7/23/26 with offering proceeds, and the term loan was repaid in March, so net debt including finance leases is ~$0.28B today and ~$1.1B at the horizon, not $0.73B. Diluted shares are ~125M, not 127M. My 41x peer median mixed developer software into the set; on one CY27 Finviz basis the infrastructure anchor is 23.7x (23.4x per supervisor), and DOCN's 55% gross margin and GPU capex make that the right anchor. FY26 consensus EPS sits above the guide, so EPS growth from the guide midpoint is ~31%. Consensus CY27 revenue is $1.81B (+53%). I also dropped the DCD '$800M' headline as a funding-risk signal, because it is most likely the March follow-on. Rebuild: P/E falls to 38x (PEG parity against the infrastructure anchor, inside the peer range) x $2.40 = $91. I added EV/EBITDA at 16x NTM $0.95B = $113. The DCF rises to $118: lower net debt and fewer shares add ~$5, the revenue path moves to consensus, and FCF now subtracts lease-funded capex so it stays consistent with the rising horizon net debt. The blend is ~$107 vs $105 in round 1, so the corrections offset. Industry lane: demand evidence is unchanged and strong (CRWV +112% with a $104B backlog, CY27 consensus revenue doubling to $26B; Akamai GPUs sold out; ~$0.8-1T 2027 hyperscaler capex). New-generation GPU rental rates are firm, while H100/H200 hold a tight band. This demand is largely already in the $1.81B consensus, so it supports hitting consensus rather than beating it. The risk lies in pricing for older GPUs and in financing sentiment. Ladder: fundamentals are below spot (~$107) but momentum and demand argue the market keeps a growth premium. I keep a 12-month median of ~$132 with a fat-tailed lognormal mix (60% sigma 0.60, 40% sigma 0.80; vs 82% realized), giving P(>=140) 0.465, P(>=210) 0.24 and P(>=70) 0.83, nearly unchanged from round 1 because the corrections net out. Research this round was limited to ~6 follow-ups: MarketScreener for DOCN and CRWV worked, the Akamai and Nebius valuation pages failed to fetch, and the GPU price trackers were secondary.
